summary: This infobox-style note summarizes the ICC Champions Trophy, a One Day International cricket tournament administered by the International Cricket Council. It lists the first tournament (1998, Bangladesh), the last (2017, England and Wales), and the next (2021, India), along with the round-robin and knockout format and team counts. It also gives the current champion Pakistan and the tournament's record holders.
one_line: The ICC Champions Trophy is a One Day International cricket tournament run by the International Cricket Council, first held in 1998.
key_facts: The ICC Champions Trophy is administered by the International Cricket Council.
The ICC Champions Trophy is a One Day International tournament.
The first ICC Champions Trophy tournament was held in 1998 in Bangladesh.
The most recent ICC Champions Trophy before the 2021 edition was held in 2017 in England and Wales.
The next ICC Champions Trophy tournament was scheduled for 2021 in India.
The tournament format is round-robin and knockout.
The tournament has had 13 teams in all tournaments and 8 teams in the most recent tournament.
The current champion is Pakistan, which won its first title.
Australia and India are the most successful teams, with two titles each.
India shared the 2002 ICC Champions Trophy with Sri Lanka.
Chris Gayle holds the record for most runs in the tournament with 791.
Kyle Mills holds the record for most wickets in the tournament with 28.
